title.en: Specreel

summary.en: According to Product Hunt, Specreel lets app teams create narrated, shareable browser demos from a URL or Playwright test traces on successful builds, using an open-source CLI plus hosted Cloud; supplied details do not establish supported workflows, licensing, or reliability.

title.en: Hybrid Reasoning Agents

summary.en: HybridAgents combine latent reasoning with text-based tool interaction via HybridLink and continuous hybrid memory; authors report across three scales and 11 benchmarks a 10.4% performance improvement plus 35.5%–54.7% token reduction, but supplied evidence lacks experimental detail and independent validation.

title.en: Redesigning source control at Anthropic

summary.en: Anthropic reportedly replaced Git with Scion and its review system Antique after merges rose from about 2,500 per day in May 2026 to over 30,000 in September, citing a roughly 100 GB main-branch history, 25 GB compressed working copies, and about 25 million daily CI checkouts; the author speculates that stronger internal models contributed.

title.en: Redesigning source control at Anthropic

summary.en: Anthropic describes redesigning source control around a git-to-Scion ingestion pipeline as its reported merge rate rose from roughly 2,500 daily changes in May 2026 to over 30,000 in September; discussion questions code-review quality, benchmark context, and retaining nearly 100 GB of main-branch history.

title.en: LIBERO-RIG: A Hardware-Setup Robustness Benchmark for Vision-Language-Action Models

summary.en: LIBERO-RIG holds LIBERO tasks fixed while varying eleven robot hardware/setup axes across 210 conditions; authors report nine VLA models’ pooled success dropping from 0.932 nominally to 0.767 at middle and 0.509 at highest severity, but real-world validation is not stated.

title.en: Tiden

summary.en: Tiden is a Product Hunt-listed tool for teams using Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or Copilot that versions intent as mergeable requirements and checks changes with tests in the user's environment, though its implementation, setup burden, and validation evidence are not provided.

title.en: Inferock

summary.en: Inferock is a Product Hunt-listed serverless LLM inference service for developers using OpenAI, Claude, or Gemini keys, offering token billing, call-failure and cost visibility, and credits for eligible failed calls; eligibility, implementation, and provider behavior are unspecified.

title.en: daily.dev

summary.en: Product Hunt describes daily.dev as a developer-news service that lets Claude, Cursor, Codex, and other MCP clients access personalized feeds, search posts, discussions, bookmarks, and feed tuning, with unspecified integration and ecosystem details.

title.en: Reason

summary.en: Product Hunt presents Reason as a cloud or local coding agent that can implement tasks, run tests, and open pull requests through Mac, terminal, web, or Slack, with model and subscription choice; its claimed evaluation and cost advantage lacks supplied validation.

title.en: Pancake

summary.en: Pancake is presented on Product Hunt as an MCP-connected GTM platform for AI-agent users, combining a “GTM Brain,” sending infrastructure, and 40+ data and enrichment providers; implementation, reliability, privacy, and pricing details are not provided.

title.en: Retriever AI

summary.en: Retriever AI is a Product Hunt-listed free browser agent for users automating lead outreach, creator shortlisting, and job applications in local Chrome or hosted cloud browsers; its claimed accuracy, speed, and cost advantages are unverified in the supplied material.

title.en: AdAnt 2.0

summary.en: Product Hunt lists AdAnt AI as a social-media marketing tool that researches niches, creates video batches, monitors X and Reddit, and schedules posts, while its claimed view and acquisition-cost results are unverified maker claims.

title.en: AirJelly

summary.en: AirJelly, presented on Product Hunt, is an always-on desktop AI agent for people managing work and personal follow-ups that claims to infer intent from on-screen activity and organize or act on tasks, with privacy, permissions, integrations, and reliability left unspecified.

title.en: Microsoft Maia 300

summary.en: Product Hunt describes Microsoft Maia 300 as a planned 2027 AI inference platform for long-context reasoning, low-latency conversation, and agents, citing HBM4, N2P chiplets, and 96-accelerator racks; specifications and efficiency claims are unverified in the supplied material.

brief.en: Research highlights and technical community discussions.
brief.zh: 研究亮点与技术社区讨论。

title.en: Hybrid Reasoning Agents

summary.en: HybridAgents combine latent reasoning with text-based tool interaction via HybridLink and continuous hybrid memory; authors report across three scales and 11 benchmarks a 10.4% performance improvement plus 35.5%–54.7% token reduction, but supplied evidence lacks experimental detail and independent validation.

title.en: LIBERO-RIG: A Hardware-Setup Robustness Benchmark for Vision-Language-Action Models

summary.en: LIBERO-RIG holds LIBERO tasks fixed while varying eleven robot hardware/setup axes across 210 conditions; authors report nine VLA models’ pooled success dropping from 0.932 nominally to 0.767 at middle and 0.509 at highest severity, but real-world validation is not stated.

title.en: ChunkAct: Action Chunking for Agentic Robotics

summary.en: ChunkAct compiles routine sub-goal primitives into autonomously executed action chunks so LLM calls scale with decisions rather than primitives; on LIBERO-Pro, the authors report 5.0-point higher success than prior agentic robotics with 2.9× fewer calls, but broader validation and experimental details are absent.

title.en: What Matters in Quality-Aware VLA Pretraining: A Benchmark and Empirical Study

summary.en: The authors introduce AXIS-Bench and compare quality weighting, filtering, and conditioning on 5,000 suboptimal demonstrations across 24 tasks, reporting higher mean success from approach-aware conditioning and real-world success rising from 9.6% to 31.7%, without abstract-level details on protocols or robustness.

title.en: Tev: Scaling Long-Horizon Agentic Environments with Dense Progress Rewards

summary.en: Tev-Gym provides 1,170 verified long-horizon task environments across seven domains and uses latent-world specifications plus progress-potential reward shaping; the authors report Tev-27B gains on ALE-CM and Terminal-Bench subsets, but missing experimental details and independent validation limit confidence.

title.en: Data Free Training of Diffusion Models for Lattice Field Theories

summary.en: The authors train diffusion samplers for 2D φ⁴ lattice theory from self-generated samples plus an unnormalized target density, reporting performance comparable to HMC-reference-data training across symmetric, critical, and broken phases; broader-model and independent validation are not supplied.

title.en: DoubtLess: Training-Free Contrastive Decoding for Efficient Reasoning

summary.en: The authors propose DoubtLess, which uses the logit difference between brief- and verbose-prompted small-model reads of a large model’s ongoing CoT to steer decoding, reporting 31% shorter Qwen3-32B CoTs and 20% fewer coding-agent thinking tokens with unchanged performance, pending independent validation.

title.en: AesCode: Aesthetic Code Generation with Decoupled Cross-Modal Rewards

summary.en: AesCode uses a design graph plus deterministic and VLM-based cross-modal rewards to train visual-artifact code generation, with authors reporting 22.4–31.1-point visual-quality gains over same-scale Qwen3-VL baselines, but missing methodological and independent validation details.

title.en: Exact Topological Compliance: Generating Persistence-Equivalent Graphs

summary.en: The authors formulate generating graphs with exactly a target persistence diagram, propose an iterative degree-based method and a complete constraint-programming encoding, report exact realization on four graph-generation benchmarks, but provide no abstract-level detail on scalability, baselines, or runtime trade-offs.

title.en: Two Clocks: Why Larger Rollout Batches Learn Slower but Fail on Schedule in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards

summary.en: The authors model RLVR with separate progress and failure sample clocks, reporting that square-root learning-rate scaling preserves first-order drift but can reduce multi-step sample efficiency beyond a critical batch; GRPO tests on Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B and other settings support this, but detailed metrics and broader validation are not provided.

title.en: MFG: Multi-turn Feedback Guided Molecular Optimization

summary.en: MFG trains an LLM with reinforcement learning, a vector of prior-turn property and similarity feedback, and a feedback-aligned reward to iteratively optimize molecules; authors report an 81.50% average similarity-constrained success rate across ten tasks versus 70.81% for GeLLM³O, without abstract-level external or experimental validation.

title.en: Scaling Online Optimal Transport Minibatches for Flow Matching

summary.en: The authors propose a scalable online entropic optimal-transport approximation for flow matching, claim proofs of lower stochastic-gradient variance and integration error than independent pairing, and report improved stability and generation performance as coupling minibatches grow, but provide no abstract-level quantitative or reproducibility detail.

title.en: Back-Translation Still Matters: Leveraging Monolingual Data for Low-Resource Machine Translation with LLMs

summary.en: The authors report that interleaving parallel-data updates with LLM back-translation from monolingual text improves translation into low-resource languages by 16–173% XCOMET-XXL over parallel-only fine-tuning across five languages and two 3B backbones, but broader reproducibility and generalization evidence is not provided here.

title.en: Statistical Vignettes on the Grokking Phenomenon

summary.en: The authors analyze grokking in a tractable setting, deriving conditions and asymptotics for delayed-generalization plateaus while separating nuisance fitting, core learning, and interpolation-edge dynamics; they report experimental agreement, but assumptions and validation details are not supplied.

title.en: Depth Memory

summary.en: The authors frame transformer depth aggregation as memory retrieval and propose Linear Depth Memory, using recursive least squares across residual, associative-memory, and inverse-covariance streams; they report lowest perplexity versus PreLN, mHC, and AttnRes at 400M and 1.5B parameters, but provide no abstract-level cost or robustness evidence.

title.en: SkillScaffold: Scaffolding Agentic Reinforcement Learning with Policy-Adaptive Skill Credit Assignment and Selective Injection

summary.en: SkillScaffold estimates reusable textual-skill utility from outcome-verified trajectories using outcome-aware likelihood comparisons, selectively injects only estimated-helpful skills, and authors report gains on ALFWorld, WebShop, ScienceWorld, and τ²-Bench, but quantitative results and evaluation details are absent here.

title.en: Registration is a Representation Problem: Solving Whole-Body PET/CT Registration

summary.en: The authors register longitudinal whole-body PET/CT by combining anatomix per-voxel semantic features with coarse segmentations in a GPU-accelerated multistage solver and lesion-volume-preserving constraints, reporting first place in Learn2Reg 2026 PSMAReg without task-specific training, though metrics and external validation are not provided.

title.en: SEAR: Self-Evolving Agentic Robotics

summary.en: SEAR benchmarks whether language-model robotics agents genuinely retain and transfer learning across 330 simulated and five physical tasks, reporting that transferable code and routines generalize better than task-specific solutions, while real-robot results lag on novel human-designed scenes; methods and baselines are not detailed here.

title.en: Who Improves the Robot? Toward Physical Recursive Self-Improvement

summary.en: The authors define Physical RSI with an L0–L5 framework, survey adaptation, training, and safety methods, and report that existing literature does not demonstrate it as defined, leaving reliable feedback, causal attribution, safety preservation, and benchmarks unvalidated priorities.

title.en: Fast Rates for Offline Q-Learning with KL Regularization

summary.en: The authors study tabular finite-horizon offline Q-learning with KL regularization, proposing KLQ and pessimistic KLPQ and claiming \(\widetilde O(1/\epsilon)\) sample complexity, with KLPQ removing KLQ’s explicit exponential dependence on regularization and horizon; proofs and empirical validation are not provided here.

title.en: RoboSimStudio: An Interactive Toolkit for Rapid Real2Sim of Robot Manipulation Tasks

summary.en: RoboSimStudio is an interactive Open Newton-based toolkit for iteratively fitting robot-manipulation simulations by exposing solver, contact-model, and physical-parameter choices, with author-described visual, force-feedback, and agentic Real2Sim2Real experiments but no supplied metrics or baseline validation.

title.en: OmniCompass: A Holistic Benchmark for Omni-Modal Video Grounding and Understanding

summary.en: OmniCompass introduces manually verified visual-language and audio-visual video benchmarks spanning temporal grounding, spatial grounding, and QA, and the authors report that 50 MLLMs struggle with precise grounding and paired-specification consistency, but the abstract omits metric, baseline, and release details.

title.en: Cepheid: Decoupling Scale from Structure for Cross-Family Motion Completion

summary.en: The authors propose Cepheid, which separates dimensionless residual-motion structure from estimated physical amplitude to complete sparse mesh motion, reporting gains over harmonic extension across evaluated and unseen families plus transfer to animal video and soft-body grasping, but detailed benchmarks and validation conditions are not supplied.

title.en: The Last Remote Sensing Model Built by Humans? Casting Any Earth Observation Task as Recursive Self-Improvement

summary.en: The authors frame EO modeling as recursive improvement by a coding agent using task-specific harnesses and verifiers, reporting state-of-the-art results on four optical, SAR, and multispectral time-series benchmarks with roughly 1% labels, but provide no metrics, baselines, or validation details here.

title.en: Joint Neural Posterior Estimation and Model Selection for Chemical Reaction Networks

summary.en: The authors propose shared 1D-CNN and set-attention summaries feeding posterior model selection and model-specific cINNs for CRN pathway discrimination and rate inference, demonstrating protodeboronation deactivation-pathway analysis, but report no quantitative baselines or generalization validation in the abstract.

title.en: Self-Evolving Agent Harness

summary.en: The authors formalize fixed-weight agent harness self-evolution across prompts, memory, workflows, code, and plugins, deriving conditional generalization, retention, and fresh-validation admission bounds, but provide no empirical results or baseline comparisons in the supplied abstract.

title.en: Optimizing Team Behavior via Extremum-seeking Control in Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning

summary.en: ADiCo uses fast diversity regulation plus a slower extremum-seeking controller driven by mean episodic return to tune behavioral diversity online; across six configurations on two cooperative MARL tasks, the authors report matching or exceeding tuned and unconstrained DiCo, without broader-task or reproducibility evidence.

title.en: Where Do LLM Ensemble Gains Come From? Decomposing Candidate Value, Diversity, and Aggregation

summary.en: The authors decompose LLM candidate gain under Direct, Single-slot, Duplicate, and Multi-candidate controls, reporting control-dependent repetition gaps on MultiHopRAG and FRAMES while finding negative candidate-context contrasts in FRAMES; broader model, task, and implementation validation is not described.

title.en: Bytes to Threats: Byte-Sequence Transformer For Malware Detection

summary.en: The authors present MalwareFormer, a raw-byte transformer for malware detection, reporting 98.35% accuracy, 98.32% balanced accuracy and macro-F1, and a 1.94% false-positive rate versus two unspecified baselines; dataset, splits, robustness, and deployment-cost validation are not provided.

title.en: Read the Room Before Your Model Generates

summary.en: The authors propose Scenario-Actor, which derives a scenario embedding from Transformer hidden states to select decoding temperature, reporting stronger goal completion and open-ended instruction following and competitive multi-turn conversation on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, without abstract-level metrics or evidence of generalization.

title.en: The EU’s next chapter in AI is agentic

summary.en: Latent Space’s robotics podcast features Dyna Robotics’ chief scientist discussing Dyna-2, world action models, and physical AI; the supplied excerpt does not provide technical methods, benchmarks, or independent confirmation of its hour-long-autonomy claim.

brief.en: Top discussions and links from Hacker News.
brief.zh: Hacker News 热门讨论与链接。

title.en: Redesigning source control at Anthropic

summary.en: Anthropic describes redesigning source control around a git-to-Scion ingestion pipeline as its reported merge rate rose from roughly 2,500 daily changes in May 2026 to over 30,000 in September; discussion questions code-review quality, benchmark context, and retaining nearly 100 GB of main-branch history.

title.en: Pg_vectorsearch: An index that is faster than pgvector's IVFFlat and HNSW

summary.en: Timescale's pg_vectorsearch presents PRISM, a quantized IVF PostgreSQL vector index claimed to outperform pgvector IVFFlat and HNSW; discussion flags a 1,968-vector-dimension cap and a PostgreSQL 18+ requirement, while noting demand for low-RAM, NVMe-oriented alternatives.

title.en: Gemini 4 Argon

summary.en: Gemini 4 Argon is presented as a new Gemini model; commenters describe strong structured prose and API experience, while one reported coding evaluation places it between Fable 5 and 5.1 without methodology.

title.en: Who Is Planting Backdoors in Ledger Crypto Wallets?

summary.en: A report alleges backdoors in Ledger crypto wallets, while commenters point to alleged physical-tampering opportunities such as easy enclosure access and exposed test pads, plus uncertainty over tracing eSIM-enabled theft infrastructure.

title.en: Show HN: Guitoro, a virtual guitar you strum with your keyboard

summary.en: Guitoro is a free no-signup browser guitar playable by keyboard, mouse, or touch with recorded instrument sounds and slowable song practice; commenters praised its completeness and classroom potential while flagging Firefox layout, Android audio distortion, and fretboard-orientation issues.

title.en: Show HN: A guided 3D Leonardo da Vinci museum, built in code

summary.en: Museum of Ages launched a free, seven-language guided WebGPU/Three.js Leonardo da Vinci tour with 17 stops, reconstructed machines and source-labeled exhibits; commenters praise the scene quality but question the constrained guided navigation and 3D-first presentation.

title.en: Switzerland proposes banning profiling-based ads to minors

summary.en: Switzerland has proposed banning profiling-based advertising to minors; discussion highlights wider Swiss advertising restrictions and argues that ad-targeting transparency could help people understand and limit privacy exposure.

title.en: Iosevka is an open-source, sans-serif and slab-serif, monospace font

summary.en: Iosevka is presented as an open-source monospace sans- and slab-serif font whose supplied discussion highlights custom TTF/TTC builds and a Parametric Type Expression Language for programmatic generation, alongside mixed views on code ligatures.

title.en: Amazon pushes up prices across the Internet

summary.en: The linked article alleges Amazon raises prices across the internet, while commenters describe Amazon’s delivery reliability as a differentiator and report shifting major purchases to manufacturers or specialist retailers over pricing and quality concerns.

title.en: Recreational Programming

summary.en: A presentation on recreational programming prompted firsthand discussion that coding for fun can foster learning but may still worsen burnout when it fails to provide restorative downtime.

title.en: TV4 postpones show after AI agent erases edited material

summary.en: TV4 reportedly postponed a season of The Challenge until 2027 after a technical failure deleted much of an edited season, while discussion notes the company denies that an AI agent caused the deletion and questions backup testing.

title.en: AOSP Source Releases Are So Late Developers Disassemble Libraries to Report Bugs

summary.en: A GitHub Android NDK issue alleges AOSP source releases are delayed enough that developers disassemble libraries to report bugs; the supplied HN comments mostly speculate about causes and advocate alternatives.

title.en: Felix Rieseberg Homepage

summary.en: Felix Rieseberg’s homepage prompted discussion of an accompanying build write-up and AI-mediated creative tooling, while one commenter reported that visiting it rapidly drove high laptop resource usage and questioned its technical value.

title.en: Show HN: How random are you?

summary.en: An HN project asks users to generate ostensibly random choices and reports predictions; commenters note people often over-alternate, while one participant questions whether visible predictions changed behavior and another tests it with Math.random.

title.en: Pulsar at ESUG 2026 (new Smalltalk IDE)

summary.en: Pulsar was presented as a new Smalltalk IDE at ESUG 2026; comments mainly affirm ESUG's expert Smalltalk community and ask for IDE visuals, without adding technical evaluation.

title.en: Eric Binnion has died

summary.en: Eric Binnion has died; commenters remember him as a developer and open-source contributor who worked in the Drupal ecosystem and helped advance WordPress, while noting his terminal diagnosis and focus on family.

title.en: Strafe: A new open-source, E2E Encrypted, and federated alternative to Discord

summary.en: Strafe presents itself as an open-source, end-to-end encrypted, federated Discord alternative, while discussion flags an apparent missing repository license and emphasizes that social-network migration—not cloning features—is the central challenge.
